exposure: Clinical history (cesarean delivery, duration of milk formula consumption, presence of early intestinal symptoms during infancy)

Colonic fecal microbiota (CFM) markers (Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, Actinomycetes, Lactobacillales, Clostridiales, Bifidobacteriales, B. fragilis, F. prausnitzii, B. longum, D. vulgaris, A. muciniphila concentrations)
cohort: The study included 39 Mexican children aged 2 to 18 years with autism spectrum disorders, comprising 18 FGIDs (+) cases and 21 FGIDs (-) controls.
finding: The study found that colonic fecal microbiota composition is a potential physiological predictor of FGID pathophysiology in a severity-dependent way in children with autism, with specific bacterial concentrations being significantly higher in patients with moderate symptoms.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly associated with the overall prevalence of functional gastrointestinal disorders.
cross-section timing: Children were between 2 and 18 years old at the time of the study.
